title: Three Seasons and One Short Brush
subtitle: 文学写作 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）
meta: 主题语境：文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）　|　核心词汇：series　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 series 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 the painter ① planned the series that no visitor in the studio would have described, and he said the planning was the whole of the season. The ② series, meaning the set itself and not the brush, ran three seasons and stayed undescribed in the book; a series, he said, is the only thing in a studio that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ series in that studio had the same short brush beside it, and the ④ series at the far easel, meaning the sketch they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A series, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the painter said the describing is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the series was the whole of the matter, meaning the order and not the set. The ⑥ series, meaning the order and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; series, he said, is either something you plan or the only word that means both a set and an order. He said the order is the part they remember.

By 1976 the ⑦ series had become a line in a catalogue, and the catalogue had become an argument about the short brush. The ⑧ series of the whole thing, the painter wrote in May, was one studio and three seasons of describing; series, he said, is either the sketch at the far easel or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ series I remember is the set described in the catalogue, which closed in 1978 and is still described as the quietest in the studio. A ⑩ series, my mother said in 1980, is the only set that improves by being described; every series, she said, is an order that has agreed to look like a set. She said the order was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 系列；连续（指画室里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 系列；连续（指那个系列本身，与小小的画笔相对）
C. 固定搭配：plan the series 策划这一个系列
D. n. 系列；连续（指留给孩子们留着的那一幅）
E. n. 系列之事（抽象总称，指一处画室的系列之事）
F. n. 系列；连续（指展品目录里写到、被描述的那一个）
G. n. 系列、次第（指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 次第（抽象总称，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: planned the series that no visitor in the studio would have described

answers.why: plan the series 意为“策划这一个系列”，1971 年那位画师把画室里没有一位观者肯描述的一个系列做了一遍。
series 意为“系列；连续”，指那个系列本身而不是小小的画笔，它经过了三个季度而在簿子上没有被描述。
series 意为“系列；连续”，指画室里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一支小小的画笔。
series 意为“系列；连续”，指最远那副画架的留给孩子们留着的那一幅，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
series 意为“系列、次第”，指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个次第就是那件事的全部。
series 意为“次第”，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个系列，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
series 意为“系列；连续”，指展品目录里写到、被描述的那一个，到 1976 年这一个成了展品目录里的一行。
series 意为“系列之事”，画师五月写道，整件事的系列之事是一处画室和三个季度的描述。
series 意为“系列；连续”，我记得的是展品目录里描述过的那一个，1978 年画成了，至今仍被说成画室里最安静的一个。
series 为抽象总称，母亲 1980 年说，系列是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的系列。
